issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual description) specifies a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void that SealSaloon.orderMeal() should call. The reference solution implements checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)). This signature difference is a structural mismatch that can confuse students (they will implement/no-arg method per the spec) or make tests that expect the no-arg method incompatible with the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification by providing a no-argument public void checkOrderReady() method. If logging is desired, add an overloaded or private helper checkOrderReady(boolean) and have the no-arg method delegate to it with a default value. Also ensure orderMeal invokes the no-arg method so it matches the problem description and UML.

issues.description: The problem specification declares a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void (UML and textual description). The reference implementation declares checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)), changing the method signature. This mismatch means the conceptual operation 'checkOrderReady' is represented with different identifiers/signatures across artifacts, which can confuse students about the exact method they must implement and may break tests or the expected API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent with the problem statement. Either change the solution to provide a no-argument method public void checkOrderReady() (for example, implement public void checkOrderReady() { checkOrderReady(true); } or move logging behind an internal/private flag), or update the problem statement and UML to declare checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging). Prefer implementing the no-arg public API so it matches the exercise specification.
